Chief Data Officer Dashboard.description: Jules Keeper's view of the data governance program at Coco Pharmaceuticals: whether the program has been built, whether the DATA domain's own metrics are moving, whether the common vocabulary is in use, whether the data hub is delivering, and where things stand against the ninety day plan and the risk register.
Chief Data Officer Dashboard.heading: How the Data Governance Program is Going
Chief Data Officer Dashboard.name: Chief Data Officer Dashboard

placements.content: **How is the data governance program going?**  Every tile below is a live query against Egeria, so this page changes as the domain teams, the data hub team and the data governance team add to the catalog.  The DATA domain exists in service of the domains that carry business and regulatory responsibility, so most tiles measure the shared foundation those domains depend on.  Where a governance metric has no live measure yet, the dashboard says so rather than leaving it out.

**1. Has the governance program been built?**  The governance definitions defined by all the governance leaders and their teams, the metrics that make them observable, and the information supply chains and blueprints that put the data in a business context.

**2. Are the DATA domain's own metrics moving?**  The data governance program defines six metrics.  Three have a live measure below: *Percentage of Data Assets with Designated Owner* (Data Asset Ownership, a direct measure), *Catalog Registration Coverage* (Governance Classification Coverage and Catalog Freshness, a partial measure until discovery scanning runs) and *Lineage Coverage for Critical Data Elements* (Solution Design Context, a proxy: the first hop from an asset to the design it implements, not an end-to-end lineage path).

**Not yet measured: data quality.**  Three of the DATA domain's metrics — *Critical Data Element Quality Expectation Coverage*, *Data Quality Rule Pass Rate* (target 98% or above) and *Open Data Quality Issues by Age* (target: nothing older than seven days on critical data) — need automated quality rule results and a record of the issues they raise.  The clinical trials pipeline in `2. clinical-trials` runs quality checks, but their results are not yet recorded in the catalog in a form these tiles can count.  Until they are, the honest answer to *how good is our data?* is *we cannot yet say*, and closing this gap is the next priority for Erin Overview and Peter Profile.

**3. Is the common vocabulary being used?**  A glossary term is only useful once it is defined, and only does its job once it is attached to the data it describes.  The first tile shows how many terms have a definition; the second shows how many terms are actually assigned to something in the catalog.

**4. Is the data hub delivering?**  The digital products that deliver critical data between systems, how the catalog has grown over the last ninety days, and the register of strategic information supply chains the company governs and monitors at company level.

**5. The plan, the risks and the metrics.**  The ninety day plan with the status of each phase and task, the company risk register built by all the governance leaders, and the full governance metric register — the metrics system the Impact Phase set out to build, of which the tiles above are the first live measures.

placements.content: **How is the data governance program going?**  Every tile below is a live query against Egeria, so this page changes as the domain teams, the data hub team and the data governance team add to the catalog.  The DATA domain exists in service of the domains that carry business and regulatory responsibility, so most tiles measure the shared foundation those domains depend on.  Where a governance metric has no live measure yet, the dashboard says so rather than leaving it out.

**1. Has the governance program been built?**  The governance definitions defined by all the governance leaders and their teams, the metrics that make them observable, and the information supply chains and blueprints that put the data in a business context.

**2. Are the DATA domain's own metrics moving?**  The data governance program defines six metrics.  Three have a live measure below: *Percentage of Data Assets with Designated Owner* (Data Asset Ownership, a direct measure), *Catalog Registration Coverage* (Governance Classification Coverage and Catalog Freshness, a partial measure until discovery scanning runs) and *Lineage Coverage for Critical Data Elements* (Solution Design Context, a proxy: the first hop from an asset to the design it implements, not an end-to-end lineage path).

**Not yet measured: data quality.**  Three of the DATA domain's metrics — *Critical Data Element Quality Expectation Coverage*, *Data Quality Rule Pass Rate* (target 98% or above) and *Open Data Quality Issues by Age* (target: nothing older than seven days on critical data) — need automated quality rule results and a record of the issues they raise.  The clinical trials pipeline in `2. clinical-trials` runs quality checks, but their results are not yet recorded in the catalog in a form these tiles can count.  Until they are, the honest answer to *how good is our data?* is *we cannot yet say*, and closing this gap is the next priority for Erin Overview and Peter Profile.

**3. Is the common vocabulary being used?**  A glossary term is only useful once it is defined, and only does its job once it is attached to the data it describes.  The first tile shows how many terms have a definition; the second shows how many terms are actually assigned to something in the catalog.

**4. Is the data hub delivering?**  The digital products that deliver critical data between systems, how the catalog has grown over the last ninety days, and the register of strategic information supply chains the company governs and monitors at company level.

**5. The plan, the risks and the metrics.**  The ninety day plan with the status of each phase and task, the company risk register built by all the governance leaders, and the full governance metric register — the metrics system the Impact Phase set out to build, of which the tiles above are the first live measures.

Analytic - Generic Metric Trend.description: Trend any analytic function over time. metric_path is the target function; metric_params are its keyword arguments. Default trends count_elements(type_name=Asset).

Analytic Demo - AI Context Readiness.description: 'cataloged' (Asset supertype count), 'documented' (Assets whose description is set and not empty), 'classified' (elements matching ANY of the same governance classifications governed_coverage uses), and 'lineage' (count of DataFlow relationships -- design/ business lineage, distinct from OpenLineage's operational lineage) are all native counts over the whole repository (including elements the viewer may not be able to see), computed as of 2026-08-01. 'aiReady' stays None from this function ALWAYS, by design -- these four are independent counts, not a per-asset check, so they can't answer 'how many assets are ALL of these at once'. See 'Analytic Demo - AI-Ready Assets' (below) for that -- a genuinely different function, not a missing field on this one. FIXED metric -- Fixed 5-stage readiness definition baked into the function body -- not a parameter. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: dict (cataloged, documented, classified, lineage, aiReady).

Analytic Demo - Active Contributors.description: Distinct usernames behind at least one feedback relationship (ratings/comments/likes/tags/noteLogs) -- pick BAR below for a by-type breakdown. A real engagement signal Feedback Summary's raw relationship counts don't give you: ten comments from one person and ten comments from ten people both show up as '10' there, but differently here. FIXED metric -- Fixed to Collaboration OMAS's feedback relationship types -- not a parameter. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: dict (contributors, byType).

Analytic Demo - Assets by Type Breakdown.description: Per-type counts across the core asset/infrastructure types -- pick BAR or PIE below for a chart, DICT/JSON for the raw {label, type, count} rows. GENERIC function -- the metric this counts is a parameter (`analytic_spec_params`), not fixed. This spec shows one example binding; copy it and change the params to count something else entirely with the same function. Result shape: list[dict] ({label, type, count}). Default params (edit/override at run time): {'type_map': [['Data Stores', 'DataStore'], ['Data Sets', 'DataSet'], ['Software Components', 'DeployedSoftwareComponent']], 'strict': True}.

Analytic Demo - Catalog Growth Trend.description: Snapshot-based growth series -- assets/terms/governed/products, one point per window step, each a native count over the whole repository (including elements the viewer may not be able to see). Run with output_format SERIES for a Vega-Lite line chart. GENERIC function -- the metric this counts is a parameter (`analytic_spec_params`), not fixed. This spec shows one example binding; copy it and change the params to count something else entirely with the same function. Result shape: list[dict] (time series: {label, date, <series_key>: count, ...}). Default params (edit/override at run time): {'window': '6mo'}.

Analytic Demo - Certifications and Excep.description: Active/expiring Certification relationships and License counts. 'exceptions' is a GENERAL open-governance-Exception count (any Exception relationship in the repository) -- it is NOT scoped to certifications/licenses specifically, despite sitting in this same summary; treat it as a separate metric riding along here. FIXED metric -- Fixed to the Certification and Exception relationship types -- not a parameter. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: dict (active, expiring90, soon, licenses, exceptions).

Analytic Demo - Contextualised Coverage.description: Percent of Assets connected to a SolutionComponent via ImplementedBy -- a proxy for 'has some solution-design context', not the literal 'participates in an ISC/blueprint'. FIXED metric -- Fixed to the ImplementedBy relationship, filtered to Asset-subtype ends -- not a parameter. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: dict (contextualisedCount, assetTotal, contextualisedPct).

Analytic Demo - Count by Property.description: Counts active DigitalProduct elements with deploymentStatus=ACTIVE. GENERIC function -- the metric this counts is a parameter (`analytic_spec_params`), not fixed. This spec shows one example binding; copy it and change the params to count something else entirely with the same function. Result shape: scalar (int). Default params (edit/override at run time): {'type_name': 'DigitalProduct', 'property_name': 'deploymentStatus', 'property_value': 'ACTIVE', 'strict': True}.

Analytic Demo - Element Count by Type.description: Counts active GlossaryTerm elements. GENERIC function -- the metric this counts is a parameter (`analytic_spec_params`), not fixed. This spec shows one example binding; copy it and change the params to count something else entirely with the same function. Result shape: scalar (int). Default params (edit/override at run time): {'type_name': 'GlossaryTerm', 'strict': True}.

Analytic Demo - Engagement Over Time.description: Weekly-bucketed feedback-event trend (comments/ratings/likes/tags/noteLogs), zero-filled across the trailing window. Run with output_format SERIES for a chart. FIXED metric -- Fixed to Collaboration OMAS's 5 feedback relationship types -- weeks tunes the window, not what's measured. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: list[dict] (time series: {week, comments, ratings, likes, tags, noteLogs, total}). Default params (edit/override at run time): {'weeks': 12}.

Analytic Demo - Feedback Summary.description: Ratings/comments/likes/tags/noteLogs counts by type -- pick BAR below for a by-type breakdown chart. A trend over time isn't available from this metric yet (feedback_summary is a point-in-time snapshot, not a series) -- a real gap for later. FIXED metric -- Fixed to Collaboration OMAS's feedback relationship types -- not a parameter. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: dict (byType, total).

Analytic Demo - Governance Coverage.description: Count of elements of ANY type that you can see carrying at least one of the five governance classifications (ZoneMembership/Confidentiality/Criticality/Impact/Retention) -- not a share of Assets, and not a percentage. It counts what the caller may see (zone security applies), by a find paged until Egeria returns an empty page, so governedCount is every governed element you can see (governedCapped is false when measured). It is not the Overview's Governed tile, which counts Assets only, natively across the whole repository, as a share of all Assets: the two numbers differ by definition. byClassification and topZones are nested breakdowns of the same elements (byClassification tallies every classification they carry, not only the five) -- pick BAR below for a chart of byClassification. FIXED metric -- Fixed to GOVERNANCE_CLASSIFICATIONS: ZoneMembership, Confidentiality, Criticality, Impact, Retention -- not a parameter. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: dict (governedCount, governedCapped, byClassification, topZones).

Analytic Demo - Karma Leaderboard.description: Top-N people by karma (ContributionRecord.karmaPoints, anchored via Anchors classification). FIXED metric -- Fixed to ContributionRecord.karmaPoints -- top_n and anchor_types tune the result but don't change what's being measured. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: list[dict] (name, karmaPoints, anchorGuid, anchorType). Default params (edit/override at run time): {'top_n': 10}.

Analytic Demo - Orphan Glossary Terms.description: Approved-but-unassigned glossary terms -- terms with no SemanticAssignment relationship to anything. orphanCount = termTotal - referencedCount. FIXED metric -- Fixed to the SemanticAssignment relationship type and GlossaryTerm elements -- not a parameter. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: dict (termTotal, referencedCount, orphanCount).

Analytic Demo - Ownership Coverage.description: Count of elements carrying an Ownership classification -- NOT a percentage, same caveat as Governance Coverage (no cheap total-elements denominator yet). The find is paged until Egeria returns an empty page, so ownershipCount is every owned element (ownershipCapped is false when measured; an incomplete scan is not measured). byOwnerType is a nested breakdown of the same ownershipCount elements by the owner's type (Person, Team, SolutionActorRole, ...) -- pick BAR below for a chart of byOwnerType. FIXED metric -- Fixed to the Ownership classification -- not a parameter. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: dict (ownershipCount, ownershipCapped, byOwnerType).

Analytic Demo - People and Community.description: Counts of Person/Team/Organization/ITProfile/Community actor profiles. FIXED metric -- Fixed to Person/Team/Organization/ITProfile/Community -- not a parameter. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: dict (persons, teams, organizations, itProfiles, communities). Default params (edit/override at run time): {'strict': True}.

Analytic Demo - Semantic Grounding.description: groundedAssets = the number of DISTINCT Assets with a glossary term on it or on any of its parts (tables, columns): a SemanticAssignment on the Asset itself, or on an element anchored to it, counts that Asset once. A deleted element grounds nothing. groundingLinksNotOnAsset = the links that ground no Asset (a term on a process, say); groundingLinksScanned = the links the scan read (the ones you can see, so it can be below groundingLinks). groundedAssetPct = that number as a percent of all Assets (groundedAssetTotal). Both are what you can see: the count comes from a scan of every SemanticAssignment, and the total is counted in the same population, so groundedAssetPct is empty, and groundedAssetNote says why, when your Asset total cannot be counted -- never a number mixing populations. groundingLinks = the number of SemanticAssignment links across the whole repository, and groundingPct = links per hundred Assets (at most 100): that is links, not Assets -- an Asset with three terms counts three times. A per-asset breakdown (which assets are or aren't grounded) isn't available from this metric -- a real gap for later. FIXED metric -- Fixed to the SemanticAssignment relationship type -- not a parameter. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: dict (groundedAssets, groundedAssetTotal, groundedAssetPct, groundedAssetNote, groundingLinksScanned, groundingLinksNotOnAsset, groundingLinks, groundingPct).

Analytic Demo - Stale Assets.description: Assets with no update in the last N days (default 180) -- candidates for archival review. FIXED metric -- Fixed to the Asset type -- population isn't a parameter, but the staleness threshold (days) is. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: dict (staleCount, assetTotal). Default params (edit/override at run time): {'days': 180}.

Analytic Demo - Term Definition Complete.description: Share of GlossaryTerms whose description is set and not empty; total and defined are native counts over the whole repository (including terms the viewer may not be able to see). undefinedPct is the gap (not the coverage) -- a near-100%-defined glossary is the uninteresting case, and the gap is what's actionable. FIXED metric -- Fixed to GlossaryTerm's description property -- not a parameter. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: dict (total, defined, undefinedPct).

FIXED metric -- Fixed to InformationSupplyChain and SolutionBlueprint -- not a parameter. This spec always returns that one metric. Result shape: dict (informationSupplyChains, blueprints). Default params (edit/override at run time): {'strict': True}.
